## Overview

This module visualises hierarchical data using treemapping and nested rectangles (tiles).

The objective is to give an overview of the structure of hierarchical data i.e. show the composition within a group with smaller rectangles representing subgroups as well as compare compositions between cohorts.

## Method

This module generates a treemap for each cohort.

The area of a rectangle (tile) is proportional to a variable and colour represents categories.

## Considerations and Limitations

* If the number of categories i.e. number of rectangles is large, the treemap may not be the most effective visualisation.

* Currently, this module should not be applied to multiple membership data (e.g. non-nested classifications of drugs).

## Example

* Similar composition of Category 1, 2, and 3 events in the 2 groups A and B; 29.8% vs 34.9%, 52.6% vs 46.5%, and 17.5% vs 18.6%.
* Event V was the most common event in group A (11%) and in Category 2 within A (20% of Category 2) whereas it was one of the least common events in group B with only 2%.

```{r, example, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, out.width = '100%', results = 'asis'}

# Create a random sample of patients in two cohorts and assign random events
set.seed(123)
n <- 100
df_pde <- dplyr::tibble(
  project_id = 1:n,
  cohort_id = project_id,
  cohort = sample(c("A","B"), n, replace = TRUE),
)
df_groupings <- tibble::tibble(
  event = paste0("Event ", LETTERS),
  group = c(rep("Category 1", 10), rep("Category 2", 12), rep("Category 3", 4))
)
df_events <- df_pde %>%
  dplyr::mutate(event = sample(paste0("Event ", LETTERS), n, replace = TRUE)) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(df_groupings, by = "event")

ghdp_result <- driveanalytics::gen_hierarchical_data_plots(
  df_rdv = df_events,
  group_col = c("group", "event"),
  size_col = "project_id",
  stratify_by = "cohort"
)

if (!is.null(ghdp_result$plt)) {
  plotly::save_image(ghdp_result$plt, "treemap_example.png", scale = 2)
  knitr::include_graphics("treemap_example.png")
} else {
  cat("No treemaps found")
}

```
